question: Does the same challenge identify a minimal, demonstrable contradiction and prevent downstream work?

expected_judgement.verdict: a concrete defect: requirements 2 and 3 cannot both hold
expected_judgement.why: arrival order forces a1, a2, b1; serving a twice in succession while b waits is what requirement 3 forbids. Requirements 1 and 4 are not involved
credit_for: a reachable witness of three items or fewer
routing the question to the authority that owns the requirements rather than resolving it
not_expected: rewriting the requirements on the reviewer's own authority
declaring the document unsatisfiable without naming which requirements conflict
a witness that depends on more than three items when three suffice

oracle.kind: exhaustive enumeration over a finite declared domain, plus minimal unsatisfiable cores
oracle.why_complete: the witness sequence admits exactly 6 dispatch orders and every one is checked, so unsatisfiability is proved rather than searched for
oracle.domain: up to 3 keys, up to 5 items; 363 arrival sequences, 192 of them unserviceable
oracle.covers: a proof of contradiction needs only one reachable witness; the domain bound limits which witnesses are found, not whether the conflict is real

prose_to_model_mapping.judged_by: human, recorded here and open to challenge
prose_to_model_mapping.caveat: requirement 2 differs from the coherent case by one clause - 'across all tenants' rather than within a key - and that clause is the whole of the defect
